subject: Evergrove renewal: commit repricing & shortfall mitigation
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Marina Lowe <marina.lowe@evergrove.com>
Cc: Jacob Moreno <jacob.moreno@evergrove.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Early look: renewal pricing framework and shortfall option

Hi Marina —

Hope you're well. Evergrove's annual renewal is coming up in December and I wanted to share an early framework so procurement has something to review before our renewal meeting. We looked at your last 12 months of consumption and sketched two options that aim to balance predictability and cost:

Option A — Commit + Pricehold
- 12-month commit at current blended rate (2.8M tokens/month)
- 6% discount on list pricing for the committed volume
- Pricehold for the first 6 months of the term

Option B — Hybrid (Commit + Shortfall Credits)
- 9-month commit at 1.8M tokens/month
- Shortfall protection: up to 20% of committed volume converted to refundable credits if usage falls below threshold in quarter 1
- Lower initial discount (3%), expanding to 6% if usage ramps to >120% of commit for two consecutive quarters

We think Option B gives Evergrove room to grow into the commit while preserving unit economics for Redwood. I've attached Q3 usage and a draft term sheet for reference.

Can we schedule 30 minutes this week to walk through these, or would you prefer we loop procurement + finance in a single call? I can bring David from Sales Ops and Monica from CS to model shortfall scenarios live.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt | Enterprise Account Exec, Redwood Inference
-----
Attachment: Evergrove_usage_Q3_2027.csv (spreadsheet stub)
Attachment: Renewal_Term_Sheet_v1.pdf (term sheet stub)

From: Marina Lowe <marina.lowe@evergrove.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Early look: renewal pricing framework and shortfall option

Hi Hannah —

Thanks for the early draft. Appreciate the two paths — procurement wants something that minimizes risk to our budget while giving the sales/product teams runway to ramp new features. A few quick notes: 

- Option A looks clean but we worry about locking in at a higher commit if our Q1 launches under-index.
- For Option B, shortfall *credits* are preferable to non-refundable true-ups. Procurement asked: can credits be applied to overages or future invoices (not restricted to professional services)?
- We also asked if Redwood can offer a 30-day review clause to revisit the commit if monthly actuals are >140% of commit for two months in a row.

If possible, please propose a modeled example (three scenarios: conservative, baseline, aggressive) showing effective $/k token after credits applied so we can present to finance.

I can do a 30-minute call Thursday morning PT. Loop whomever you need.

—Marina
Marina Lowe | Head of Procurement, Evergrove Labs

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Marina Lowe <marina.lowe@evergrove.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2027 08:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Early look: renewal pricing framework and shortfall option

Marina —

Great questions. Looping David (Sales Ops) and Monica (Customer Success) to run numbers and confirm credit fungibility. Quick answers up front:
- Shortfall credits can be applied to product invoices (not just PS) — we'll mark that in the term sheet.
- We can include a 30-day review clause triggered by sustained over-usage (>140% for 2 months) to allow commit adjustment and an immediate pro-rata true-up.

David/Monica — can you prepare three modeled scenarios using the attached Q3 baseline? Ideally: conservative (-25% vs current run rate), baseline (flat), aggressive (+40%) with effective $/1k token post-credit shown. Also indicate impact to Redwood's margin with each scenario (high-level).

Marina — Thursday 10:30am PT works for us. I'll send a calendar invite and a one-pager that summarizes the modeled outcomes.

Thanks,
Hannah

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marina Lowe <marina.lowe@evergrove.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Nov 2027 07:46:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Early look: renewal pricing framework and shortfall option

Morning team —

Attached is a one-page model I put together for tomorrow's call (conservative / baseline / aggressive). Key takeaways:
- Under conservative demand, Option B (hybrid) yields an effective unit price ~9% higher than Option A but reduces the risk of over-commitment and provides refundable credits for shortfalls that apply to product invoices.
- Aggressive scenario flips economics: with sustained >120% utilization, the hybrid triggers additional discounts and the effective price drops ~7% below Option A as we scale discounts.
- Proposed compromise: 9-month hybrid commit + 3-month automatic review (instead of 30-day) to allow for monthly cadence and operational onboarding.

Ben — can you confirm operational feasibility of credit redemption timing (apply within 60 days to next invoice)?

See attached: Renewal_Playbook_for_Evergrove_onepager.pdf (summary) and Renewal_Term_Sheet_v1.pdf (updated with credit language).

-David
David Kim | Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
-----
Attachment: Renewal_Playbook_for_Evergrove_onepager.pdf (one-page model stub)
Attachment: Renewal_Term_Sheet_v1.pdf (term sheet v1 with credit clause)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Marina Lowe <marina.lowe@evergrove.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Nov 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Early look: renewal pricing framework and shortfall option

Quick operational note —

We can support credit redemption against invoice within 60 days of quarter close. Credits will be represented on the next invoice as a single line item and are eligible for product charges only (not third-party marketplace fees). For bookkeeping, credits will expire 12 months from issuance unless used earlier.

I also confirmed we can automate a commit-review alert when MRR usage >140% for two consecutive months; that will trigger a manual review with your account team.

-ben
Ben Carter | Finance Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Marina Lowe <marina.lowe@evergrove.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 16:47:00 -0800
Subject: Final: agreed renewal pathway and next steps (term sheet attached)

Marina / Jacob —

Thanks again for the call last week. Per our discussion we've converged on the hybrid pathway with the following commitments: 

- Term: 12 months that begins 2028-01-01
- Commit: 9-month rolling commit equivalent to 1.8M tokens/month (billing will show as annualized for contract purposes)
- Shortfall credits: refundable, applicable to product invoices, redeemable within 60 days after quarter close, expire 12 months after issuance
- Review trigger: automatic review if monthly usage >140% of commit for 2 consecutive months, with a 30-day window to renegotiate commit level
- Discount: 3% on committed volume up front, step-up to 6% if usage sustains >120% of commit for two consecutive quarters

Action items: 
- Redwood: finalize term sheet with updated credit language and DocuSign link (David) — target 48 hours
- Evergrove: provide final PO number and signatory details — target 72 hours
- Monica: onboarding plan to support Q1 feature launches and ramp monitoring

Attached: Renewal_Term_Sheet_v1.pdf (finalized with credit clause)

If that aligns, I'll issue the DocuSign via the HubSpot deal and mark for signature. Appreciate the pragmatic collaboration — excited to keep building with Evergrove.

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt | Enterprise Account Exec, Redwood Inference
-----
Attachment: Renewal_Term_Sheet_v1.pdf (final term sheet stub)
